intro.title: Websites that work for the people who use them
intro.lead: Three chapters of WordPress and front-end work: an educational membership charity, small-business clients and a B2B music platform. Each story shows the problem, what I did, who I worked with and what changed.
intro.note: Learning on Screen is a rights-focused educational charity, so I don't keep copies of work that belongs to them. The Learning on Screen screenshots are of public pages, taken from copies archived by the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine. Some embedded videos don't play in the archive.

chapters.name: Learning on Screen
chapters.headline: Collections and publishing tools for a membership charity
chapters.teaser: Migrated broadcast collections onto one accessible platform and gave the marketing and content teams the WordPress tools to publish on their own.
intro: Learning on Screen (the British Universities and Colleges Film and Video Council) is an educational charity that works with around 200 member institutions in higher, further and school education. Its services include Box of Broadcasts (BoB), an on-demand TV and radio service, and TRILT, an index of UK broadcast listings covering more than 560 channels from 1923 onwards.
I joined a small Agile development team and grew into a role that sat between development, marketing and content, UX, and the membership team who work with students, academics and researchers.

situation.text: The broadcast collections lived on the older BUFVC site, with a different look and navigation from the main Learning on Screen website.

stories.title: Giving the marketing and content teams the tools to publish

situation.text: The marketing and content teams needed to build and update pages themselves, but the WordPress theme didn't have the building blocks they needed. At the same time, an external agency was redesigning the main website.

task.text: Fill the gaps in the platform and make sure colleagues could publish confidently once the new site launched.

action.text: Built reusable components editors could add to any page: hero, tiles, cards, accordion, tabs and video player.
Integrated Advanced Custom Fields, MailerLite sign-ups, Google Tag Manager and cookie consent.
Coordinated reviews of the agency's work with the content strategist and marketing specialist through Jira, Teams and meetings, and handled the handover with our tech lead.
Trained marketing colleagues to publish content in WordPress.

result.text: The content team could build and publish pages without waiting for a developer.

chapters.highlight: Live site restored within an hour

stories.title: Keeping a B2B marketing site running, and building its replacement

situation.text: I Like Music licenses music to broadcasters, businesses and schools. Its WordPress marketing site was live and business-critical, and a relaunch was planned.

task.text: Manage and extend the live site, and design and build the new one.

action.text: Extended the site with custom templates and fields (Elementor, Gravity Forms, ACF), enquiry forms to email and LinkedIn tracking.
When a CAPTCHA plugin update crashed the site because it needed a newer PHP version, diagnosed the cause and fixed it with our DevOps engineer.
Agreed requirements for the relaunch with the client services team, designed it in Figma and built it. It hasn't launched yet, so I describe it here rather than show it.

result.text: The live site was back online within an hour, and plugin updates are now checked on staging first. The relaunch site is complete and ready for launch.
